newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANDY JOHNSON WINS AGAIN AS MARINERS EDGE RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANDY JOHNSON WINS AGAIN AS MARINERS EDGE RANGERS.

text.p: Randy Johnson allowed just four hits over seven innings to notch his 11th win and Paul Sorrento and Jay Buhner homered as the Seattle Mariners edged the Texas Rangers 2-1 on Thursday.
In recording his sixth consecutive victory, Johnson (11-1) gave up one unearned run, walked one and struck out six to bring his American League-leading strikeout total to 138.
"He's pitching very good baseball for us," said Seattle manager Lou Piniella. "He got a little tired but he pitched out of some tough situations. He is the best pitcher in baseball."
Bobby Ayala allowed one hit, walked two and struck out one in two scoreless innings of relief to pick up his fifth save and preserve Johnson's 22nd win in his last 23 decisions.
Ken Hill (4-5) gave up two runs and nine hits over 7 1/3 innings to take the loss as the Rangers fell two games behind the first-place Mariners in the West.

With one out in the second, Sorrento sent Hill's 1-2 pitch over the right-field fence for his 11th homer. Buhner led off the seventh and hit a 1-1 pitch over the left-field wall for his 18th homer and a 2-0 lead.
Texas scored its run in the bottom of the inning when Juan Gonzalez singled and later scored on an error by Seattle left fielder Rob Ducey.
In Anaheim, Garret Anderson's two-run single with one-out in the bottom of the ninth inning lifted the Angels to a 4-3 victory over the Oakland Athletics.
The A's had taken a 3-2 lead in the top of the ninth when first baseman Jim Leyritz misplayed Damon Mashore's grounder, allowing Rafael Bournigal to score.
But the Angels loaded the bases in the bottom of the ninth with one out.
Daren Erstad led off with a single off Oakland closer Billy Taylor (2-4). Orlando Palmeiro walked and Taylor then hit Leyritz with an 0-2 pitch to load the bases.
Mike Mohler relieved Taylor and Anderson lined a 1-1 pitch into left-centre field, scoring Erstad and Palmeiro with the tying and winning runs as the Angels snapped a five-game skid.
Geronimo Berroa's two-run single in the third put Oakland ahead 2-0. Anaheim tied it with single runs in the third and sixth innings.
